acceptanceResults: A first-class repository-bound command can append a contract_amendment_revalidation successor decision for an archived Work Item whose current archived Contract digest differs from the historical verification evidence digest.

The revalidation receipt binds the current archive manifest, current Contract/Summary/Outcome/Events bytes, historical verification evidence bytes, repository identity, current Runtime identity, successor identity, and explicit human authority without rewriting predecessor bytes.
Missing, malformed, foreign, stale, symlink-backed, contradictory, or digest-mismatched archive/evidence inputs fail closed with stable recovery errors and no partial successor or receipt.

A revalidation successor can be activated while its predecessor remains pending close, can run fresh verification against the current Contract, and can complete its own verified terminal lifecycle; the predecessor pending-close gate is cleared only after the successor has a valid archived terminal boundary and human close decision.
Predecessor close, Outcome, status, and recovery projections distinguish historical evidence from current revalidation and retain an auditable link to the successor and human decision.

Rust protocol/repository/CLI tests cover amended Contract, stale predecessor receipt, evidence tamper, manifest tamper, symlink, repository isolation, and successor lifecycle behavior; existing recovery and legacy compatibility tests remain passing.

English, Simplified Chinese, and Japanese command/workflow documentation describe the append-only revalidation boundary, exact command/help surface, immutable predecessor bytes, and no-hand-edit rule.
